class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">5-year high</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Developer tooling sentiment</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>Scott MacVicar, Head of Developer Infrastructure at Stripe, has one big recommendation for engineering leaders who are rolling out AI with their teams: accelerate.</p>
<p>&quot;My advice for anyone thinking about trying AI coding is, move faster on this,&quot; he said.</p>
<p>Stripe itself adopted Cursor quickly but carefully. The company is known for 99.9999% API uptime and products that set the bar for developer experience. They couldn&#x27;t sacrifice either.</p>
<p>The key was getting all of Stripe&#x27;s more than 3,000 engineers started within the right guardrails. Stripe preloaded Cursor on every machine, used Cursor Rules to provide codebase context, and adapted code review practices to maintain quality at higher velocity. Along the way, they also discovered something unexpected about who was getting the most value from AI.</p>
<h2 id="setting-engineers-up-for-success" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#setting-engineers-up-for-success" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Setting engineers up for success</h2>
<p>Stripe had high conviction early on that AI would fundamentally change how its engineers work. The question was how to manage that shift across more than 3,000 developers. The approach they took: Make Cursor work well for everyone from day one.</p>
<p>&quot;When people start, they&#x27;ve got VS Code, IntelliJ, and Cursor all installed on their machines, and they go through a lab that teaches them how to use the Stripe developer environment,&quot; said MacVicar.</p>
<p>Everything is preconfigured. Stripe uses Cursor Rules to give Cursor context about Stripe&#x27;s codebase and coding standards. They&#x27;ve empowered teams to add their own rules too, while calibrating as an organization on how comprehensive to make them. This approach has allowed Stripe&#x27;s developers to become productive with AI coding tools on day one and then go even further from there.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">One of the things we&#x27;ve prided ourselves on is the ability for engineers on their first day to ship a PR. When people start using Cursor, they have an optimal experience as we&#x27;ve lowered the barrier to entry and the barrier to adoption.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Scott MacVicar</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Infrastructure, Stripe</div></div></div></div>
<p>Cursor adoption spread through an influencer system. Power users shared their workflows in lunch-and-learns, showing teammates how to run multiple agents in parallel or write better prompts.</p>
<h2 id="adapting-code-review-for-ai-coding" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#adapting-code-review-for-ai-coding" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Adapting code review for AI coding</h2>
<p>AI allowed engineers to write more code. But that wasn&#x27;t the goal. Stripe didn&#x27;t want higher velocity to mean lower quality. Their solution was adapting code review to keep pace.</p>
<p>Stripe now uses LLMs to help reviewers work more efficiently. AI flags complex methods or risky files, directing reviewers&#x27; attention where it&#x27;s needed most. Engineers have also gotten more comfortable pushing back on code that isn&#x27;t ready, whether it came from a person or an agent.</p>
<p>Stripe engineers have embraced this new way of working: On an internal survey, developer sentiment recently hit a five-year high. MacVicar said, &quot;People are really excited about the tools they&#x27;re getting.&quot;</p>
<h2 id="the-tenure-advantage" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#the-tenure-advantage" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>The tenure advantage</h2>
<p>Stripe is now focused on helping engineers get the most value they can from Cursor. The early findings have surprised MacVicar. He expected junior engineers to benefit most, using AI to compensate for limited experience. Instead, he&#x27;s seen the longest-tenured engineers make the biggest productivity gains.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">People who have been at Stripe for a long time have the context in their heads. They&#x27;re able to clearly see what they want to achieve and direct agents to do it.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Scott MacVicar</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Infrastructure, Stripe</div></div></div></div>
<p>In response, MacVicar is exploring whether new hires should spend their first weeks learning the codebase before getting Cursor access. They could use that time to build up the context needed to get the most out of AI tools.</p>
<p>It&#x27;s one example of why MacVicar advises other engineering leaders not to wait to have everything figured out with AI. Many of the most important questions they&#x27;ll need to answer only emerge once engineers are actually using the tools. He sees getting started now as the best way to optimize for both present possibilities and the future of software engineering.</p>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re interested in accelerating your engineering team&#x27;s adoption of agentic coding workflows, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to get started with a Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">5-year high</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Developer tooling sentiment</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>Scott MacVicar, Head of Developer Infrastructure at Stripe, has one big recommendation for engineering leaders who are rolling out AI with their teams: accelerate.</p>
<p>&quot;My advice for anyone thinking about trying AI coding is, move faster on this,&quot; he said.</p>
<p>Stripe itself adopted Cursor quickly but carefully. The company is known for 99.9999% API uptime and products that set the bar for developer experience. They couldn&#x27;t sacrifice either.</p>
<p>The key was getting all of Stripe&#x27;s more than 3,000 engineers started within the right guardrails. Stripe preloaded Cursor on every machine, used Cursor Rules to provide codebase context, and adapted code review practices to maintain quality at higher velocity. Along the way, they also discovered something unexpected about who was getting the most value from AI.</p>
<h2 id="setting-engineers-up-for-success" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#setting-engineers-up-for-success" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Setting engineers up for success</h2>
<p>Stripe had high conviction early on that AI would fundamentally change how its engineers work. The question was how to manage that shift across more than 3,000 developers. The approach they took: Make Cursor work well for everyone from day one.</p>
<p>&quot;When people start, they&#x27;ve got VS Code, IntelliJ, and Cursor all installed on their machines, and they go through a lab that teaches them how to use the Stripe developer environment,&quot; said MacVicar.</p>
<p>Everything is preconfigured. Stripe uses Cursor Rules to give Cursor context about Stripe&#x27;s codebase and coding standards. They&#x27;ve empowered teams to add their own rules too, while calibrating as an organization on how comprehensive to make them. This approach has allowed Stripe&#x27;s developers to become productive with AI coding tools on day one and then go even further from there.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">One of the things we&#x27;ve prided ourselves on is the ability for engineers on their first day to ship a PR. When people start using Cursor, they have an optimal experience as we&#x27;ve lowered the barrier to entry and the barrier to adoption.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Scott MacVicar</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Infrastructure, Stripe</div></div></div></div>
<p>Cursor adoption spread through an influencer system. Power users shared their workflows in lunch-and-learns, showing teammates how to run multiple agents in parallel or write better prompts.</p>
<h2 id="adapting-code-review-for-ai-coding" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#adapting-code-review-for-ai-coding" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Adapting code review for AI coding</h2>
<p>AI allowed engineers to write more code. But that wasn&#x27;t the goal. Stripe didn&#x27;t want higher velocity to mean lower quality. Their solution was adapting code review to keep pace.</p>
<p>Stripe now uses LLMs to help reviewers work more efficiently. AI flags complex methods or risky files, directing reviewers&#x27; attention where it&#x27;s needed most. Engineers have also gotten more comfortable pushing back on code that isn&#x27;t ready, whether it came from a person or an agent.</p>
<p>Stripe engineers have embraced this new way of working: On an internal survey, developer sentiment recently hit a five-year high. MacVicar said, &quot;People are really excited about the tools they&#x27;re getting.&quot;</p>
<h2 id="the-tenure-advantage" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#the-tenure-advantage" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>The tenure advantage</h2>
<p>Stripe is now focused on helping engineers get the most value they can from Cursor. The early findings have surprised MacVicar. He expected junior engineers to benefit most, using AI to compensate for limited experience. Instead, he&#x27;s seen the longest-tenured engineers make the biggest productivity gains.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">People who have been at Stripe for a long time have the context in their heads. They&#x27;re able to clearly see what they want to achieve and direct agents to do it.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Scott MacVicar</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">Head of Developer Infrastructure, Stripe</div></div></div></div>
<p>In response, MacVicar is exploring whether new hires should spend their first weeks learning the codebase before getting Cursor access. They could use that time to build up the context needed to get the most out of AI tools.</p>
<p>It&#x27;s one example of why MacVicar advises other engineering leaders not to wait to have everything figured out with AI. Many of the most important questions they&#x27;ll need to answer only emerge once engineers are actually using the tools. He sees getting started now as the best way to optimize for both present possibilities and the future of software engineering.</p>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re interested in accelerating your engineering team&#x27;s adoption of agentic coding workflows, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to get started with a Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- -->
